newsitem.title: INDIA: India Hindalco sees marginal fall in net.
newsitem.headline: India Hindalco sees marginal fall in net.

text.p: India's largest private aluminium maker Hindalco said on Wednesday it expected a marginal decline in its 1996/97 (April-March) net profit due to power problems and low global aluminium prices.
Hindalco's net profit in the financial year ended March 31, 1996, was 4.01 billion rupees ($112 million).

"The decline is on account of power disturbance caused by a grid failure in April 1996 which resulted in a production loss of about 7,000 metric tonnes (MT)," Hindalco said in a written response to questions from Reuters.
Hindalco said aluminium output in 1996/97 was expected to fall to around 167,000 tonnes from 175,398 tonnes in 1995/96.
It said alumina output would also fall below the previous year. "We anticipate alumina production to be close to 330,000 MT in 1996/97 as compared to 341,000 MT in the previous year."
"Other factors such as the planned shutdown of our rolling mill for the purpose of modernisation, and low international prices of aluminium also had an impact on net profit," it said.
Global aluminium prices hit a two-and-a-half year low of just below $1,300 a tonne on the London Metals Exchange last October, before reversing a prolonged downtrend.
"The general expectation is that there will be a consolidation of recent price gain," Hindalco said, adding that the firm was optimistic about prices in calendar 1997 and beyond.
It targeted aluminium production of 210,000 tonnes in 1997/98, with exports at 10-15 percent of total production.
The firm said it was planning a review and withdrawal of discounts that it had offered customers to combat increased imports due to the plunge in international prices.
The company added that it had been offering discounts of up to 7.5 percent on its products.
Hindalco said it was exploring plans to set up new smelting capacity.

"Tentatively we are considering a 250,000 MTPA (tonnes per annum) smelter, supported by an alumina refinery with initial capacity of 500,000 MTPA and power generation capacity of 600 MW," the firm said.
The firm said it had not yet decided on a site for the smelter, although it was likely to be near bauxite and coal mines.

Hindalco said it was pleased with proposals like share buybacks and lower taxes announced in the 1997/98 federal budget on February 28. The company did not say whether it planned to buy back its own shares.
It said the increase in import duty on unwrought aluminium to 20 percent from 10 percent had "provided the aluminium industry a long sought measure of relief".
"The impact of the increase in import duty will be reduced pressure on prices."
